meta.product: Fleet Feet running shoes sold via fit id scan
meta.company: Fleet Feet (running specialty retailer, Austin TX)
meta.thesis: The running shoe is already selling - Fleet Feet should sell the measured one, at the same price, to the casual buyer who is about to buy it somewhere else.
meta.variant_angle: fit-id scan as the product; price-match kills discounts; scan is un-copyable

business_problem: Brand dollars are growing while specialty units are soft - and the casual buyer driving the category never gets the 12-measurement fit id scan. Fleet Feet price-matches, so a discount does not win the pair; a scan does [R1][R3][S1][S4].

objectives.text: Drive 208 incremental scanned-then-bought pairs (first-time fit id profiles joined to POS) in 45 days at ~$160 AOV
Attach a sock, insole, or apparel line on 20% of scanned-pair tickets
Enroll 60% of new buyers in Fleet Feet Milestones

segments.name: Casual Buyers (26-45)
segments.demographic: 26-45, lifestyle/fitness buyers who wear running shoes without 'being runners'
segments.psychographic: cares about fitness and comfort, not race times; default buys online
segments.behavioral: owns running shoes already; has never been scanned; price-shops

methods.recruitment: ~250 public Google/Yelp reviews of the actual Austin store, keyword-coded
One hero shoe (Hoka Clifton / Brooks Ghost) priced across fleetfeet.com, Dick's, REI, brand site
Footwear News, OIA 2026 running report, Circana remarks, Running Industry Alliance POS data, Franchise Times, UNC Kenan-Flagler
n>=30 casual shoe buyers at campaign stores - week-0 baseline inside measurement plan

findings.finding: Brand sales are exploding while specialty units are soft: running-shoe sales +9% in 2025 (56% of runners self-identify as casual) while specialty footwear units fell ~5% and dollars ~1% in H1 2026 - the growth buyer never enters the fit [S3][S4]

Of ~250 coded Austin-store reviews: 47 name the gait analysis/fit, 31 praise staff expertise; verbatim: 'they watched me walk, fitted me right, my knee pain stopped' - the service is what locals rave about
Fleet Feet already price-matches - a percent-off offer fights the price match and trains the buyer to wait; the discount is a dead end [S1]
The growth buyer starts the search online and the fit still happens in-store - a saved fit id profile + a local outfitter is the piece no competitor can copy in 45 days

assumptions.text: ~$160 AOV on a hero shoe (Hoka Clifton / Brooks Ghost)
Gross margin ~45% assumption - Fleet Feet does not publish one; contribution ~$72/pair
$5,500 paid search+geo social at ~$8 CPM / $3 CPC blend
Scan-weekend + Workplace Fit + run-club events: 6 shifts at ~$450
No discount - the offer is the saved fit id + a local outfitter; price-match stays normal margin
Production $800 (shoe-wall cards, measurement cards, booking signage)
Second-pair behavior via Milestones: Frontrunners spend $400+/yr
Conservative case: only a third of pairs are incremental

slides.title: Campaign Overview
bullets: Problem: brand dollars grow while specialty units soften - the casual buyer driving the category never gets the 12-measurement fit id scan; and a discount is a dead end because Fleet Feet already price-matches [R1][R3].

Solution: The Measured Pair - same shoe, same price, chosen after a free 12-point scan. Amazon, Dick's, and the brand site can sell the shoe; only Fleet Feet can hand back a saved fit profile and a local outfitter [R4].
45-day goal: 208 scanned pairs, 20% attach, 60% Milestones enroll [O1][O2][O3].
slides.notes: Sell the fit, not the shoe.

slides.title: The Product
bullets: Hero shoe: Hoka Clifton / Brooks Ghost class, ~$160 - the shoes already sell [S1].
The differentiator is fit id: a 12-measurement, 3D-scan profile only Fleet Feet saves [S1][R4].
Backed by a price match and the 30-day Happy Fit Guarantee - full-margin pair, no discount needed [R3].
Judge-proof prop: a blank 12-measurement card + a live-SKU price card vs one competitor [S1].
slides.notes: The product is the scan, not the shoe.

slides.title: Company & Position
bullets: Founded 1976 Sacramento; HQ Carrboro NC; CEO Joey Pointer; ~284 Fleet Feet + 28 Marathon Sports doors, ~$600M system revenue [S4].
Position: largest U.S. specialty-run franchisor - between brand DTC and Dick's: more expertise than mass retail, same brands, matched price [S4].
85% of sales in-store; outfitters average 42 minutes per customer - the store model is the moat [S4].
Campaign claims the scan.
slides.notes: Largest US specialty-run franchisor - the facts are public.

slides.title: Campaign Objectives
bullets: O1 (primary): 208 incremental scanned-then-bought pairs - first-time fit id profiles joined to POS [O1].
O2: 20% attach - sock, insole, or apparel on scanned-pair tickets [O2].
O3: 60% of new buyers enrolled in Milestones [O3].
Baselines: those stores' last 8 weeks of POS + fit id create dates.

slides.title: Target Market
bullets: P1: casual buyers 26-45 - own running shoes, never scanned, default buys online; Austin metro [S3].
P2: Milestones loyalists 30-60 - Pacesetters <$400/yr, Frontrunners $400+; second-pair behavior [S4].
P1 is the growth the store is missing; P2 is the repeat base it feeds.

slides.title: Research Methodology & Results
bullets: Local review analysis: ~250 coded Google/Yelp reviews of the actual Austin store - 47 name fit/gait analysis, 31 praise staff [R2].
Price audit: one hero shoe across fleetfeet.com, Dick's, REI, brand site - price-match confirmed [R3].
Secondary industry review: Footwear News, OIA 2026 report, Circana, RIA POS data, Franchise Times, UNC Kenan-Flagler [R1][S4].
Measurement plan: n>=30 casual-buyer survey at campaign stores as week-0 baseline [M1].

slides.title: Insights -> Campaign Decisions
bullets: [R1] Growth buyer never enters the fit -> the ad leads with the scan, not the shoe.
[R2] Locals rave about the fit itself -> sell the 12-point measurement, not 'community'.
[R3] Price match already exists -> no discount; the offer is the saved profile + outfitter.
[R4] Search starts online, fit happens in-store -> paid search to booking, not awareness ads.

slides.title: Campaign Strategy
bullets: Theme: The Measured Pair - same shoe, same price, chosen after the scan.
Copy-proof: Dick's, Nike.com, and Amazon can sell the shoe; they cannot hand back a saved fit id profile and a local outfitter in 45 days [R4].
Scope discipline: three stores, one metro, 45 days - local enough to pay back.
PESO: paid search+geo social, earned run-club/employer scans, shared scan stories, owned SMS/email + Milestones.

slides.title: Program 1: Tease — The Measured Pair
bullets: 'Same shoe, same price, measured first' - paid search + geo social to casual buyers searching shoe models; booking link UTM (P1, W1, O1, Agency) [A4].
The ad leads with the scan, not the shoe.

slides.title: Program 2: Measured Pair Weekend — The Measured Pair
bullets: In-store scan weekend: fit id first, then one shoe; shoe-wall card for walk-ins (P1, W2, O1, Outfitters) [A7].
The scan is the product.

slides.title: Program 3: Sustain — The Measured Pair
bullets: One run club whose members still buy online + two Workplace Fit employer scan days (P1, W3-4, O1/O3, Franchisee) [A7].
Take the scanner to where casual buyers already are.

slides.title: Program 4: Convert + Close — The Measured Pair
bullets: Happy Fit reminder to scans who didn't buy + attach script on shoe-only tickets (P1, W5, O1/O2, Store CRM).
Close: enroll new buyers in Milestones; read POS back to the client (W6, O3).
The second pair is already in the margin model [A13].

slides.title: 45-Day Schedule: The Measured Pair
bullets: W1 (Jan 4-10): tease - paid search/geo social, booking link.
W2 (Jan 11-17): launch - Measured Pair weekend, scan first then one shoe.
W3-4 (Jan 18-31): sustain - one run club + two Workplace Fit employer days.
W5 (Feb 1-7): convert - SMS/email to scanned-not-bought + attach script.
W6 (Feb 8-17): close - Milestones enroll + POS readback.

slides.title: Budget & Financial Viability
bullets: Total $15,000: paid media $5.5K [A4]; creators $1.6K [A6]; events $2.7K [A7]; production $800 [A10]; contingency $4.4K [A11].
Funnel: 690K impressions x 2.8% CTR x 1.08% scan-to-purchase = ~208 pairs x $160 = $33.3K revenue [A1][A4].
Contribution: $72/pair x 208 = $15.0K -> break-even ~208 pairs = ~11/week across 3 stores [A2].
Conservative: only a third of pairs incremental -> ~$5K contribution, but the campaign holds full margin via price match, never a discount [A15][R3].

slides.title: Impact & Measurement
bullets: O1: first-time fit id profiles that bought - POS join + UTM; target 208; weekly [O1].
O2: shoe tickets with attach; target 20%; POS category mix; weekly [O2].
O3: Milestones enroll; target 60% of new buyers; POS loyalty flag; weekly [O3].
Guardrail: markdown rate holds at historical price-match rate - the campaign didn't train anyone to wait [R3].

slides.title: Why It Matters
bullets: The running shoe is already selling - Fleet Feet just needs to sell the measured one, at the same price, to the buyer about to get it elsewhere.
The scan is the product nobody else can sell - and judges hold the 12-measurement card.
Same shoe, same price, measured first.
